steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Yu Cheng... That is the truth behind the Grand Preceptor case you seek.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Do you have any further questions?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: You've spoken at length, yet you've said nothing about your role in these events, Mr. Ning.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Why did you send someone to kill the Minister of Justice?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Do you not already have the answer, Deputy Minister Yu? Was it not you who accused me years ago of having the Minister murdered to stop him from investigating and save myself in the chaos?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: You need not be in such a hurry to discredit yourself.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: There was one question that perplexed me for a long time. Why did Gu Quan stay at your house when he returned to Baizao nearly a decade later?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: It was not until I saw that girl at your house did all the puzzle pieces fall into place.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: He narrowly escaped with his life, yet he still returned to Baizao, not only to find the truth of what happened, but also to search for the daughter he left behind.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: It seems he did not tell you much.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Yes. Most of what follows will be mere speculation. If I'm wrong, feel free to laugh in my face.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I heard that after the Grand Preceptor's suicide following accusations of treason, the entire nation was in uproar and mandarins distanced themselves from her. Yet, one Academy student dared to honor her in public.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: It was thus that he stumbled onto the Grand Preceptor's home as the belongings within were being confiscated. In his hurry, all he could take away was a baby girl, just born into the family. As it so happened, his own daughter was recently born as well.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: At his wit's end, he tried to flee Baizao with his wife and the two babies. As a scholar with no background, he didn't get far before an Imperial Guard captured him.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Perhaps out of compassion and wanting to keep the Grand Preceptor's bloodline going, the Imperial Guard spared the scholar and the Grand Preceptor's child, instead taking the scholar's daughter.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I do not know what Gu Quan was thinking at the time, but it was most likely he had no other choice.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: This child fell into the hands of the Minister of Justice, her bloodline obvious with a modicum of research. But as it turned out, how to handle this child of an outsider was a delicate conundrum indeed.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: It was around this time that you, Mr. Ning, long dissatisfied with the Minister's extreme methods, decided to take the ultimate risk: assassination.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: The Grand Preceptor's case implicated many, and it seemed fitting that the bloodstained Minister of Justice met his end through retribution. With the court's turmoil resolved, the True Lung allowed the bloodstained curtain to finally fall in this fashion.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: The only unresolved question left is that child. Based on how things are now, she was taken into your care. What this entailed is not hard to guess. But as for the why of it...

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: If I recall correctly, Mr. Ning, you enjoyed the tutelage of the Grand Preceptor as well, correct?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: O Yu Cheng, had you not been absorbed in Judicial work or confined to this cell, I shudder to think what that meticulous mind of yours might have accomplished.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: It's terrifying, truly terrifying.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: You flatter me. I'm nothing more than a fool compared to Gu Quan. It is simply because I have met far too many people in my capacity as Deputy Minister of the Judicial Review Office. The more one sees, the more one learns.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Now that I think about it, the dish Gu Quan offered to the True Lung at the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies wasn't merely an act of suicide—it was him reconciling with the truth.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Before he passed, he did not tell me the truth, but he did divulge the whereabouts of the Grand Preceptor's orphan. He must have hoped that once I found the truth for myself, I would also choose reconciliation.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Yet I could not.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: All I could do was use my methods to find the people still left, the ones you care for, and force you to spit out the truth.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: All things considered, Mr. Ning, you are no villain, perhaps just a coward...

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Hate me all you want.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: To see that child once more has always been a wish of mine...

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I will go and seek an audience with His Majesty.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You... You know everything?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I only just found out...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I still want to ask you—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: How are you... so calm about all this...?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: It was a suspicion I hid away in my heart for many, many years... One I have finally found proof for.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Like a thorn stuck in your palm. It may bleed a bit when you pluck it out, but you'll feel much better afterward.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Why...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Why won't you say something?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I don't know how it came to all this...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Should I feel sad or angry right now...?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I don't know... All I know is that my mind's a mess and my heart feels like it's being stabbed... Who the hell am I supposed to set ablaze with this fire crawling up my throat?!

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Well, I have a question for you.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Blaze... Can you tell me about Gu Quan? My... my father. What sort of man was he?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: He... He was an idiot, a nerd, and a liar!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I hate lies! I've seen too damn many of them! Greedy lies, cowardly lies, sneaky lies...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: But never one that demanded a lifetime of commitment, one that cost him his own daughter and himself, all to protect someone who had nothing to do with him.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: How... How could he be so stupid?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: It reminds me of a story I once read...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: There once was a guard who watched over a rest station by the river. One day, he saw a flood coming from upstream. He wanted to run upstream and tell the people there to close the sluice gates.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: But he had only run halfway when he saw the river was rising too quickly. It was too late to close the gates. So he immediately decided to turn and warn the villagers downstream to flee.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Back and forth he ran, until finally he was consumed and swept away by the flood. He didn't manage to do anything or save anyone.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Get to the point already...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Would you... Would you say this man's deeds sound familiar?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Fine, I get it! Well, I don't really get all the details of your windy-ass story, but you're talking shit about him, aren't you?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: He wasn't a bad guy, okay?! He was just... Urgh!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I know you've got good reasons to blame him, duh, but if he was the one who threw you away, why would he spend so much time coming back to look for you—

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I thought I would be the one consoling you, not the other way around...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Blaze... You're infected, right?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Wait, when did you figure that out—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Man, you're too... you're too damn clever by half!

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Sorry, I didn't mean anything untoward... I was just thinking that it really should have been my fate to be...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: The hell are you even talking about?!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What? You think you've done something wrong and deserve a worse fate?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Please, my life is awesome. I've got lots of buddies, and I've found a dream of mine...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: If anything, you're the one who got it bad! Growing up all by yourself in that big old mansion, alone and miserable.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: It almost sounds like you're roasting me...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I'm not—

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: But I understand... I understand what you mean.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Oh, right... I still haven't asked you what your name actually is.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Zhuhuang... Gu Zhuhuang. It's the name Dad... he gave me.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Wow... I forget how long it's been since I last told someone my real name.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Well, that's it. That's the last of my secrets.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: 'A blazing candle to ward against the dark'... Zhu for a candle, Huang for a blaze, and the family name Gu to ward you. It really does sound like a name he would pick.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Blaze... Would you say I've only really gotten to know you now, after all this?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I... I guess so, yeah.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Wait, no, I've still got lots to tell you, and I need to bring you to Victoria to have a look around. My mom—err, or rather... your birth mother. You should probably go see her...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: ...She's still alive?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Who said she was dead?! She's still hale and hearty! She lives in a small town out in western Victoria.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Once everything's wrapped up here, I'll take you to her.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Sh-She definitely wants to see you...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: A-Alright...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Why're you crying?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I-I'm not...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: But you... You're the one who's about to break into tears any second now...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I'm just... happy.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I never thought I'd suddenly find myself a little sister after all these years.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Who's ever heard of sisters like us...?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: And besides, we don't know yet who's the little one.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I've been through a lot today. Can't you let me have this one?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: And there you were, consoling me...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Look, I just wanted to say...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: From now on, you're not alone anymore, okay?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Man... Isn't that lovely?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Out of the myriad flavors in this land, the taste of reunion is the sweetest of them all.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Really, now... Dammit, what am I tearing up for...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: That's the last of my worries settled.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Oh, right, that Judicial officer at the Forbidden City last night...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Leizi...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: She was being held up by that Imperial Guard lady when she sent me flying out of the City.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: What should we do now?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: This isn't over quite yet...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I need to go and finish off what I should have done in the first place.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: You... What are you planning to do?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Demand an explanation... for everyone's sake.
One hundred years it has been.
He returns once again, to where this game of weiqi started.
The board is covered in cobwebs and dust, a single black stone at the center.
He extends his hand to brush away the grime.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Where you off to?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Got a meal to deliver.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: If you're going, then who's going to mind the restaurant?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: At this hour? It's past closing time.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Gonna open tomorrow?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: That depends on my mood tomorrow. Hard to say right now.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Why do I get the feeling that you want to call it quits?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Fine by me, but you still owe me six months of wages. Settle that and I'll let you go.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Tsch... You're so money-minded! How about all those staff meals I cooked for you, they must be worth a few months of debt...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Fine, fine... On the right of the stove in the kitchen, the third brick from the corner. The last of my spare cash is under that brick. Take it.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: I've been with you for quite a few years now.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Yep, fifteen whole years. You've stuck around the longest out of all your associates, Candleholder. Means we were really fated to be, haha.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: If I kept reminding myself that I was a Candleholder of the Sui Regulator, I'm afraid I wouldn't have stayed that long.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: *sigh* To be honest, it's been years since I reminded myself who I really am too.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Not like I was trying to remember or not, mind you. Whether as a man or beast, I've found this life full of delightful flavors. Nothing to complain about.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Best you keep not remembering.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: I fear if you do, you'll forget the tastes of man. Your palate will grow dull and numb, and your cooking skills will go to waste.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: *sigh*... Yeah, I wouldn't be too happy with that either.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: But if there's one thing I'll never forget, it's that my trouble-making brothers and sisters still need to eat.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Not to mention the one that's most troublesome of all... Though considering how long it's been since we last saw each other, it's hard to say what he's like now.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: You know the consequences of delivering this particular meal today, right?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Uh... Yeah, more or less.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: It's obvious, like not keeping cotton by the stove. The Sui Regulator's not going to be happy if we have a family reunion.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Also, if a fight breaks out at such a delicate moment, you might not be seeing me tomorrow.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: *sigh*... I've made a lot of food and met a lot of people these past few years.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: My wish was for every customer who walks through those doors to have a tasty meal and a life with fewer regrets.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: The four flavors of the kitchen. The four emotions of the heart. Sorrowful partings and joyful reunions. They're not that much different.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: But just as fresh fins have their bones and maluses have no scent, this land is filled with regrets.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Eat when you're hungry, sleep when you're tired... and when you miss your family, maybe it's as simple as going to them.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Are... Are you really willing to let this go...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: There are a lot of things I don't want to let go of, but I can't hold onto them forever either.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Jiang... Mind looking after the shop for me while I'm gone?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You've been watching me cook for so long, you must have picked something up by now. If any customers come by, look after them for me, will you?

steps.name: Yu
steps.text: 'Savors at Yu's', the 'House of Aftertaste'... It ended up being a fitting name.

steps.name: Yu
steps.text: The mortal realm really lingers on the tongue.

steps.name: Patrolling Soldier
steps.text: Captain, my report. The Patrol Battalion has dispatched all their men, and sweep searches are underway in eight districts. Still no sign of the target.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: It's been an entire day...

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Before day breaks, we must—
Heard you were looking for me?

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Who's there?!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Out of the way.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: What's this? Here to surrender?

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Good, you've saved me the effort of searching the entire city for you.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I don't care if you want to take me in for what I did at the Feast or who I am... Now's not the time for it.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I've got urgent business, so best you move it.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Hah...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I've never been this pissed off before. If you really want to get in my way, then come and try me.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: ...What are you going to do?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I'm here to deliver a bowl of longevity noodles to the True Lung.
